title: Intel Raises $20 Billion in Upsized Share Sale to Fund AI Expansion
excerpt: The chipmaker issued 210.5 million shares at $95 each after investor demand topped $100 billion, marking its first stock offering since going public in 1971.
body:
• Intel upsized its share offering from $15 billion to $20 billion, pricing 210.5 million shares at $95 each — a 2.6% discount to Monday's close.
  • Investor demand exceeded $100 billion, according to Bloomberg, and the deal could grow further if underwriters exercise their over-allotment option for an additional 31.6 million shares.
  • Proceeds will fund capital expenditures now forecast above $20 billion for 2026 as Intel races to build out foundry capacity amid surging AI compute demand.

Intel raised $20 billion through an upsized share offering on Tuesday, its first equity sale since the chipmaker went public in 1971, as it moves to capitalize on a stock rally fueled by its turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan to fund an aggressive expansion of its contract chip manufacturing business.

The company originally announced plans to raise $15 billion on Monday but increased the offering to $20 billion overnight after demand from investors surpassed $100 billion, Bloomberg reported. Intel priced the deal at $95 per share, a 2.6% discount to Monday's closing price of $97.52.

Why Intel Needs the Capital

Intel is spending heavily to transform itself into a competitive foundry operator capable of challenging Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. in contract chip manufacturing. The company raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast from $18 billion to more than $20 billion during its July earnings call, citing surging demand for processors driven by unprecedented investment in AI compute infrastructure.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Id3WY4zzLt8

The chipmaker's free cash flow has been deeply negative — a cumulative negative $44 billion between 2022 and 2025, according to FactSet — as it pours money into new fabrication facilities and advanced packaging capabilities. Its foundry unit continues to book billions in quarterly losses.

"As a capital-intensive business that went a long way to wrecking its own balance sheet and prospects by focusing on financial engineering rather than physical engineering, courtesy of $82 billion of share buybacks in the 2010s, it makes perfect sense for Intel to raise money, especially after a five-fold increase in the stock price since last August."

— Russ Mould, Investment Director, AJ Bell

Market Reaction and Stock Performance

Intel shares fell 4.1% on Monday when the company first disclosed the fundraising plan, closing at $97.52 and giving it a market capitalization of roughly $492 billion. Shares slid an additional 1.3% in premarket trading on Tuesday as investors digested the dilution.

Despite the near-term pressure, Intel's stock has been one of the market's strongest performers this year, surging more than 160% and nearly tripling from its starting point — outperforming both AMD and Nvidia as well as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which itself has gained nearly 75%.

"While the dilution is a negative for current investors, the demand signal is positive for Intel, its peers, and capital equipment suppliers."

— Matt Bryson, Analyst, KeyBanc

Foundry Ambitions and Key Customers

Intel has committed to high-volume production of chips using its 14A manufacturing process in 2028, after previously warning the technology could be shelved without a major external customer. The foundry unit has since landed Tesla as a 14A customer, and optimism for another marquee client grew after President Donald Trump said Apple would manufacture processors with Intel, though neither company has confirmed the arrangement.

Last month, Intel announced a €5 billion ($5.77 billion) investment to upgrade and expand chip manufacturing in Ireland, a project representing more than 25% of its planned 2026 capital spending.

Deal Structure and What's Next

JPMorgan Securities, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup Global Markets are acting as joint book-running managers for the offering, which is expected to close on August 12. Intel has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 31.6 million additional shares at the offering price, which could push total proceeds beyond $20 billion.

The shift toward AI agents has powered demand for central processing units beyond Intel's current manufacturing capacity. With the fresh capital in hand, Intel will look to accelerate its buildout to capture a share of the expanding foundry market before competitors lock in long-term customer commitments.
author: Diaspora Desk
